text: Every system property you'll ever touch is really the same thing underneath: a single record in the sys_properties table, storing a name, a value, a description, and a type — string, true or false, an integer, or a comma-separated list.

Underneath every Properties page you've ever opened, incident management properties, catalog properties, notification properties, you're looking at a filtered, formatted view over rows in that one table. The UI groups related properties and gives each one a friendly label and description text.

There are two ways to reach a property, and they edit the exact same record. The friendly way is an application's own Properties page, with labels, help text, and the right input control already laid out. The raw way is opening the sys_properties table directly and filtering by name — the only option for properties that have real effect but no dedicated page, which is actually most of them, since ServiceNow ships hundreds of properties and builds dedicated screens for only a fraction.

Three real properties worth knowing by name. glide.ui.incident_default_state sets the state a brand-new incident opens in. glide.sys.default_tz sets the instance's default time zone for users without a personal preference. And across almost every application, you'll find feature-toggle properties — plain booleans that switch a specific behavior on or off, with no code involved at all.

A script reads a property with one call: gs.getProperty, passing the property's name, which returns whatever value is currently stored. A developer writes that call once inside a Business Rule or Script Include, and an admin can change the resulting behavior later just by editing the property record — no code deployment required.

Because editing a property needs no scripting and no extra approval step, it's tempting to treat every property as low-risk. But a property like the default time zone or a validation toggle can affect every user or every record on the instance the moment you hit save. Next up: scheduled jobs, and how they're genuinely different from a Business Rule.
